title: From Which Day the Idle Days of an Air Ticket Fare Brands Credit Are Counted
content:
On an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking that carries a return date, the days a traveller's credit has stood unused are counted from a different day according to whether the fare brand makes its credits transferable.

## 1. Where the count starts

1.1 Where the fare brand makes its credits transferable and the booking carries a return date, the days the credit has stood unused are counted from the day the outbound was due to depart.

1.2 Where the fare brand does not make its credits transferable and the booking carries a return date, they are counted from the day the cancellation was confirmed.

1.3 In every other case no such re-anchoring of the count is made.

In both of the first two the count runs forward to today, and in both the booking must carry a return date; a one-way booking never falls on either.

## 2. Condition matrix

| Brand makes credits transferable | Booking carries a return date | The count starts from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | the day the outbound was due to depart |
| no | yes | the day the cancellation was confirmed |
| either | no | no such re-anchoring |

## 3. Worked days, on hypothetical dates

A return booking whose outbound was due to depart 210 days ago and whose cancellation was confirmed 260 days ago, held in a brand that makes its credits transferable: the count starts from the outbound departure day and comes to 210 days.

The same booking held in a brand that does not make its credits transferable: the count starts from the day the cancellation was confirmed and comes to 260 days.

A one-way booking on either brand falls to the third case, and no such re-anchoring is made.
